notes.swatch: The swatch uses the CSS variable; the hex beside it is copied from the spec. If they look different, the token is wrong.
notes.overline: Label style with the overline class. English is uppercase with letter spacing; Chinese keeps normal case and no spacing.
notes.motion: Hover or focus the tiles to see each duration. With reduced motion on, bloom drops to a 150ms fade and ambient loops stop.
notes.safeArea: This page's frame is padded by the safe-area insets and is at least 100dvh tall. On a Face ID iPhone the tinted strips show the notch and home-indicator insets.
notes.widths: Each bar is one GARDEN_CONTENT_WIDTH tier: full width on iPhone, capped on iPad.
notes.fonts: DM Sans (body) with Be Vietnam Pro for Vietnamese letters DM Sans lacks, and Fraunces with the optical-size axis (display). All three are self-hosted woff2 files, the same ones the canvas references were rendered with.

public.metaTitle: Learn English Vocabulary in 5 Minutes a Day | Dygo Academy
public.metaDescription: Learn English vocabulary with clear meanings, IPA, audio and real examples in your language. Spaced repetition brings words back before you forget. Start free.
public.metaKeywords: learn English vocabulary, English vocabulary app, English words with examples, spaced repetition, IPA pronunciation, English flashcards, vocabulary builder

hero.title: Learn a word. Use it right. Remember it for good.
hero.lead: Every word comes with real example sentences and a clear explanation in your language. Dygo brings it back just before you’d forget it. Five minutes a day is enough.
hero.languages: Available in English, Tiếng Việt and 简体中文

pains.title: How to remember English vocabulary for a long time
pains.lead: New words fade fast when you don’t see them again. Tap a card to see what helps them stay.
pains.hint: Tap to see how Dygo helps

use.front: “I know what it means, but I can’t use it.”
use.back: Every word comes with real example sentences, synonyms and fill-in-the-blank practice.

forget.front: “I learn a word today and forget it by next week.”
forget.back: Dygo brings each word back right before you’d forget it.

language.back: See meanings in Vietnamese or Chinese when you need them. Switch to English only whenever you’re ready.

habit.front: “I start strong, then give up after three days.”
habit.back: It’s five minutes and three small missions a day. On busy days, the rain barrel keeps your streak going.

how.title: How spaced repetition helps English learners
how.lead: Spaced repetition shows you each word again just before you’d forget it, and waits a little longer each time. Think of every word as a plant. Each time you remember it, it grows, and Dygo waits a bit longer before the next watering.

seed.name: Seed
seed.means: A new word you’ve just added.
seed.reviews: none yet. It’s waiting for you.
seed.grows: you study it for the first time.

sprout.name: Sprout
sprout.reviews: often, later that day or the next day.
sprout.grows: you get it right a couple of times.

flower.name: Flower
flower.reviews: every few days, then every week or two.
flower.grows: you keep getting it right as the gaps get longer.

fruiting.name: Fruiting
fruiting.grows: you keep remembering it. Most words get here after about four good reviews.

spread.title: Reviews spread out as a word grows
spread.text: Seeing a word again right before you’d forget it is what makes it stick. That way your five minutes go to the words that need them.

chart.label: Memory of a word over a few weeks: without review it fades fast; with Dygo each review brings it back and it fades more slowly each time.

drop.title: A water drop means: review it today
drop.text: When a word is due, Dygo puts a water drop on it. Review the words with a drop and you’re done. No planning needed.

forgot.title: Forgot one? That’s normal.
forgot.text: It goes back to being a sprout and comes round a few more times until it sticks.

uses.title: What do you need English for?
uses.lead: Grow the words you’ll actually use.
uses.soonLine: In the meantime, start with your own words.

missions.text: Three small missions a day. Finish all three for a Golden Bloom. On busy days, the rain barrel keeps your streak safe.

shared.title: Shared gardens
shared.text: Learn with your class or friends. Everyone sees how the group is doing, and no one sees your scores.

language.title: Your language
language.text: See meanings in Vietnamese or Chinese when you want them, or stay in English when you don’t.

parents.title: A garden for kids is on the way
parents.lead: We’re building a garden where children learn their first English words with pictures and sounds. Big buttons, short sessions, and instructions in Vietnamese and English.

points.pictures: Picture quizzes: tap the word you hear
points.faces: Two simple faces instead of a rating scale
points.stars: Bees and stars instead of red crosses
points.account: You set up and run your child’s garden from your own account

free.a: Yes. It’s free to start, and you don’t need a card.

who.a: Anyone who wants to learn English words and feel sure using them, for work, study, travel or everyday life.

english.q: Do I need to be good at English to start?
english.a: No. Dygo can explain words in Vietnamese or Chinese whenever you need it.

phone.q: Does it work on my phone?
phone.a: Yes. It runs in the browser on iPhone, Android, iPad and computers, and you can add it to your home screen like an app.

time.q: How much time do I need?
time.a: About five minutes a day. Dygo shows you which words need watering today.

ownWords.q: Can I add my own words?
ownWords.a: Yes. Add any word to “My own words” and review it like the rest.

kids.q: Is there a version for children?
kids.a: A garden for kids is on the way. For now, you can sign up on your own if you’re 16 or older. Younger learners need a parent or guardian to set up and manage their account.

speaking.q: How does speaking practice work? Do you keep my voice?
speaking.a: You listen to a recording of a native speaker saying a sentence with your word, then say it yourself. Dygo compares the two and shows you what to work on. Your recording is used only for that check and then deleted. We don’t keep it.

speak.title: How to practice English speaking on your own
speak.lead: You don’t need a partner to practice speaking. Listen, say it, then compare. Dygo puts your voice next to a native speaker’s recording, so you can see the difference instead of guessing.

listen.title: Listen
listen.text: Hear a native speaker say one real sentence. Slow it down to 0.75× if you like.

say.title: Say it
say.text: 3 · 2 · 1 · beep, then say it your way. Take as long as you need.

compare.title: Compare
compare.text: See your voice next to theirs, and the one sound to work on next.

speak.grows: Your best try helps the word’s plant grow too, so speaking counts toward your daily missions.
speak.privacy: We use your recording only to check it, then delete it.
